title: How many bars would the space data need as columns?
description: The space data of 13 years and 4 lines is imagined as a clustered column graph. The video counts the clusters, counts the columns in each cluster and multiplies. It breaks Keeko's doubt that the number of bars is found by adding.
teaching_notes: One idea: clusters of equal size are counted by multiplying the number of clusters by the columns in each cluster. Watch for students who add the two counts.

source: How many bars would a clustered column graph of the space da
video_script.why: The child has read the space line graph but has not yet seen why the same data as columns would be crowded.
video_script.substitution: Count the years to get the clusters, count the lines to get the columns in a cluster, then multiply.
video_script.anchor: the book's line graph of the number of objects launched into space each year
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko adds the number of clusters and the number of columns instead of counting the columns in every cluster.
video_script.payoff_line: such a graph needs fifty two bars

final_answer.spoken: such a graph needs fifty two bars

maths_rules: four lines (World, United States, China, Russia) give 4 columns in each cluster
slip: 13 + 4 = 17 counts the clusters and the columns of one cluster once, not every bar
a line graph shows the same data with 4 lines, so it is easier to read than 52 bars
video_script.design: One idea: equal clusters are counted by multiplying. The wrong idea is adding. The space graph stays on screen; a few clusters of four columns are drawn and the dots show the rest.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; the space line graph with the years 2012 to 2024 and four lines: World, United States, China, Russia

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears
marks.lines: the space line graph appears with its four lines
marks.ask: a crowd of columns is sketched in ghost lines behind the graph, with a question mark

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='lines'/>The space graph has four lines and the years from two thousand twelve to two thousand twenty four.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Imagine drawing the same data with columns, in a group for each year. How many bars would we need?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board; Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko appears at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: three clusters of four columns drawn side by side for three years; the words clustered column graph under them

marks.group: three groups of four columns appear, one group for each year
marks.name: the words clustered column graph are written under the groups
marks.same: every group is shown with the same four columns

narration: <bookmark mark='group'/>Put the columns of one year together in a group.
<bookmark mark='name'/>A graph with a group of columns for each year is called a clustered column graph.
<bookmark mark='same'/>Every group holds the same columns, one for each line.

beats.on_screen: Given: the years 2012 to 2024; the lines World, United States, China, Russia

marks.given: the years and the four line names are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the years from two thousand twelve to two thousand twenty four, and four lines.

beats.on_screen: To find: the number of bars in all

marks.find: the task is written under the given

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find how many bars there would be in all.

marks.yrs: the years from 2012 to 2024 are counted one by one

narration: <bookmark mark='yrs'/>Step one, count the groups. There is one group for each year, and we count both the first and the last year.
<bookmark mark='grp'/>The years from two thousand twelve to two thousand twenty four make thirteen groups.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: columns in each group = 4 (World, United States, China, Russia)

marks.cols: the four column names are written

narration: <bookmark mark='cols'/>Step two, count the columns in one group. There is one column for each line.
<bookmark mark='four'/>The World, the United States, China and Russia make four columns in every group.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: bars in all = 13 groups x 4 columns = 13 x 4

marks.mult: the product is written as 13 times 4

narration: <bookmark mark='mult'/>Step three, every group has four bars, so we multiply.
Thirteen groups, with four bars in each group.

marks.crowd: all 52 bars are drawn tightly, then the four lines of the line graph appear beside them

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Such a graph needs fifty two bars.
<bookmark mark='crowd'/>That is a crowd of columns, so the four lines are easier to read.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the groups of columns
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: a single group of four columns lit, with the other twelve groups dimmed; the single group repeated thirteen times

marks.doubt: one group of four columns is lit and the other groups are dimmed
marks.rest: the lit group is struck out as the only count
marks.again: the group of four is copied across all thirteen places

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks there are seventeen bars, by adding the thirteen groups and the four columns.
<bookmark mark='rest'/>But that counts the four columns of only one group.
<bookmark mark='again'/>Each of the thirteen groups has its own four columns, so we count four, thirteen times.
